newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium won't veto SGB's Tractebel deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgium won't veto SGB's Tractebel deal.

text.p: Belgian Economics Minister Elio Di Rupo said on Wednesday he would not use government powers to block plans by Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) to increase its stake in utility holding Tractebel.
In a statement Di Rupo said, however, that he would favour seeing Belgium's three regional companies take stakes in Tractebel's capital.

"(The minister) believes it is primordial that Belgian interests are defended within the company. Elio Di Rupo would, for example, favour a presence of the three regional (public) investment companies among Tractebel's shareholders," it said.
The Belgian government has an extensive say in how the country's gas and electricity sectors develop.
In the case of gas distribution company Distrigas, which is controlled by Tractebel, the government can veto all decisions that would be against public interest.
Tractebel also controls Electrabel, Belgium's biggest electricity company.
Di Rupo said, however, that SGB's decision to increase its stake in Tractebel to at least 65 percent from 40 percent "will not in any manner threaten the general interest".
